description:
Define the KeyService trait before any implementation is written. All code that touches DEKs depends on this trait, not on a concrete AWS KMS type. This enables the local test backend and keeps KMS behind a seam.

## Trait definition (crates/mail/src/crypto/key_service.rs)

  #[async_trait]
  pub trait KeyService: Send + Sync {
      /// Wrap (encrypt) a plaintext DEK under the site master key.
      /// Returns an opaque blob — callers must not interpret it.
      async fn wrap_dek(&self, plaintext_dek: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, KeyServiceError>;

      /// Unwrap (decrypt) a previously wrapped DEK.
      async fn unwrap_dek(&self, wrapped_dek: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, KeyServiceError>;
  }

  #[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
  pub enum KeyServiceError {
      #[error("KMS unavailable: {0}")]
      Unavailable(String),
      #[error("decryption failed")]
      DecryptFailed,
      #[error("invalid wrapped key")]
      InvalidKey,
  }

## Two implementations required by this epic

  1. AwsKmsKeyService — production
     Calls KMS Encrypt / Decrypt with the configured key ARN.
     Lives behind the existing 'aws' Cargo feature.

  2. LocalKeyService — dev and test
     Wraps with AES-256-GCM using a fixed in-process key (random at startup).
     Never persists anything. Suitable for cargo test and local dev.
     Must NOT be compiled into a release binary (cfg(test) or dev feature only).

## Why thiserror not Box<dyn Error>
  Callers need to distinguish Unavailable (retry/503) from DecryptFailed
  (likely data corruption, log and alert). Box<dyn Error> loses that.

## Acceptance
  - Trait compiles
  - Both implementations compile with their respective feature flags
  - A unit test exercises wrap → unwrap roundtrip on both implementations
title: Design: key_service trait — DEK wrap/unwrap abstraction
